title: One fleet component owns every MCP server; names are host-wide
A server process is untrusted: the host starts it, confines it by default and stops its tree
An outage keeps the tool list and fails calls honestly; nothing is replayed
MCP tools are ordinary declared tools; third-party text is bounded, labelled and deferred
The MCP client is the foundation of computer use; the harness is an MCP server only on stdio, to the program that started it
Authorisation is explicit, owned by the fleet, and kept in the credential store
Language servers: a routed seam, overlapping read-only queries, and a tool that does not ask the model to count UTF-16
The web seam: selection is configuration, availability is one check, a search may partly succeed
A model-chosen address is classified before and at connection; private means ask, metadata means no
Connectors are data over existing capabilities; nothing is downloaded by loading one
Character-set detection for fetched pages (header, byte-order mark, HTML meta prescan) with golang.org/x/net/html/charset
verified: go list -m -json golang.org/x/net@latest and LICENSE and html/charset/charset.go in the module cache, 2026-11-18; its go.mod requires golang.org/x/text v0.44.0 (BSD-3-Clause, checked the same way)

title: One package speaks MCP, over pipes the host owns or over HTTP
Servers are started, confined, supervised, restarted and stopped by one fleet
A server's tools, instructions and resources reach the model through the pipeline, and reach a seam provider through a handle
A person links, re-links and unlinks an account on a protected MCP server
The model navigates code through language servers the host owns
web_search and web_fetch stay the same whatever backend answers
A fetch cannot reach a forbidden address, follow a hostile redirect or send a credential
The vendor's search and fetch API is a provider behind the seam
A server's prompt templates are human commands
Search through the vendor's model-backed search tool, with an honest answer when no source arrives
A user turns on a connector and links its account
One child start per MCP connection, revision negotiated or pinned, no capability advertised, and Close reports whether the end was confirmed
MCP failures map to a closed set of kinds, listing stops at the page cap, task-required tools are flagged and only one package imports the SDK
Fleet reconcile touches only the changed entry, a registered entry ends with its registrant, overrides apply and a name collision is refused
Reconnect backoff and budget on a fake clock; tools stay listed in an outage and a rebuild and leave as a set; an unconfirmed stop blocks replacement
A server start carries the resolved policy, an opt-out is reported unconfined, no backend means unavailable, and no resolved secret reaches a status, error or log
Public tool names are a pure function with a hash on lossy input, and a tool generation is applied whole or not at all
Through the real pipeline a call cut off mid-flight reports outcome unknown and is never sent twice, and each other failure gives its own code
MCP result blocks map by type and model capability, instructions are labelled and bounded, an oversized generation is deferred, and an unexposed server serves only its handle
Resource tools are offered only with a connected resource-capable server, list across servers, obey restrictions and describe binary content
OAuth against fake servers: connections never start a flow, state and issuer are checked, refresh is serialised, sign-out revokes and deletes, and no secret appears in any text
Account views come from configuration and saved grants: a failed entry, an orphaned grant and a needs-reauthorisation phase are each shown
The language-server seam registers atomically, routes an overlapping extension by configuration, reports status and fails as unavailable with no provider
The stdio language-server provider overlaps queries on counted open documents, retries once after a crash, stops when idle and refuses edits
The lsp tool converts a character column or a symbol name correctly around characters outside the basic plane, caps its output and refuses a path that leaves the workspace
Web provider selection follows its table with no fallback, Check returns reasons, and a step whose provider is unusable does not carry the tool
Web result texts match golden files with the untrusted line; partial search failure, the unit budget, hidden-content removal, the span neutraliser and the depth guard hold
The destination guard refuses private, mapped, rebinding, redirected and metadata addresses, asks for loopback with an origin scope, and obeys a denied network policy
The HTTP fetch provider enforces URL rules, same-origin redirects, no credentials, byte and character caps, content-type classes and charset detection
The vendor search and fetch providers map results, pace and retry once on a rate limit, send no prompt text by default, and withhold the tool after a rejected credential
Connector presets, CLI account operations and skill-set installation behave within their limits, and loading a skill set makes no network request
Language-server symbols and diagnostics are bounded, diagnostics are fresh or marked stale, and no edit request is sent
An MCP prompt template is a scoped human command whose rendered text becomes a labelled user message; no subscription is requested
Model-backed search parses sources from structured blocks only and flags an answer without sources
The search region control is applied or reported ignored under one schema; a fetched PDF within the bound is kept as an attachment
Real stdio MCP servers are listed, called, killed, reconnected and stopped
A confined server cannot write outside its roots, and a killed host leaves no server
A hosted service is linked through a real browser, used, and unlinked
Real language servers answer navigation queries in two languages
Fetch reaches the public web through a real proxy and refuses private and metadata addresses
Search and fetch through the real vendor service, and no tool without a credential
A real browser MCP server serves one agent through an unexposed handle and returns an image
Model-backed search against the real vendor endpoint, sourced or not
A stdio MCP server runs with the host user's full authority; only its environment is scrubbed, and the SDK, not the host, starts it
A server's tool descriptions and schemas enter every request with no size bound; one hosted server's definitions total about 214,500 characters

reason: The host starts every stdio MCP server through the one starter under a policy from the sandbox resolver, by default workspace-write with only its state directory and declared roots; an unconfined server needs an explicit operator setting and is reported as unconfined.

A generation whose schemas exceed maxSchemaBytes is registered with summary disclosure, allowTools and denyTools narrow what is registered at all, and server instructions are refused above maxInstructionBytes and labelled as third-party text.

The per-server bridge is kept in Go form: the mcp/conn wrapper over the official Go SDK, a child fiber per server that supervises the connection, and a bridge that registers tools under the same mcp__server__tool names with whole-generation swaps.

The live fleet with configured and registered entries, status, restart and probe is the mcp component itself; there is no separate manager above client instances because a child fiber per server gives the same lifetimes.
The scoped provider registry disappears because resource reads are methods of the server handle; the three shared tools are kept as a separate tool component over the fleet service.
The adapter that mapped manager states to an account section becomes a read-only account view computed by the fleet from configuration and saved grants; the page is rendered by the settings UI area.
The language-server seam is kept as a contract package with a provider registry keyed by extension and four closed operations, with a route table and a status query added.

The generic stdio provider is kept: one process per provider, world and workspace root, started lazily through the host's starter under a sandbox policy, with overlapping read-only queries and an idle stop.
The lsp tool is kept with the same four operations and output caps; its position arguments change to a character column or a symbol name.

The web seam is kept as a contract and service with two provider registries and execution-time selection; availability and readiness become one context-taking check and the route preference becomes configuration.
web_search and web_fetch are kept with the same names, arguments and result texts, the HTML converter of the turndown library specification, and partial success for multi-query searches.
The anonymous HTTP fetch provider is kept with its caps and same-origin redirect rule, built on the egress client factory, and gains the destination guard and charset detection.

The vendor Search and Fetch API providers are kept behind the seam with the same provider ids and billing settings; the user's prompt is no longer sent by default and a fetch result no longer invents a status.
The model-backed search provider is kept at lower priority, with its auxiliary request logged before it is sent, its endpoint derived from the route by default and no literal key in configuration.
A package per hosted service is replaced by one generic hosted-connector component whose presets are embedded data; the linear preset supplies the URL, the display name and the naming sentence.
The Notion package differs from Linear's in a URL and a name, so it becomes the notion preset of the same generic hosted-connector component.

The service that holds registered vendor CLIs is kept: it tells the model the absolute path in runtime context and runs account commands one at a time through the host starter, with per-registration limits.

The pin by repository, commit, size and digest and the verification before publishing are kept, but the download when a plugin loads is replaced by an explicit operator install command or a local directory.
The Go harness exposes the same tool; its server argument becomes optional and it is offered only while a connected server advertises resources.
The Go harness exposes the same tool; without a server argument it lists every visible resource-capable server in bounded sections.
The Go harness exposes the same tool with server and uri; an image blob is projected as an image and other binary content as a description.
The Go harness exposes lsp with the same four operations; the cursor is given as a line with a character column counted in characters or a symbol name, instead of a UTF-16 column.
The Go harness exposes web_fetch with the single url argument and the same result text, behind the destination checks of the fetch safety decision.
The Go harness exposes web_search with the same queries argument and result text, adding one line per failed query when a search partly succeeds.
The typed notify key mcp.StatusChanged carries the server name and its status after the status cell changes; listeners cannot hold up lifecycle work, which is why the parallel form becomes notify.
The typed notify key web.ProvidersChanged is sent with no payload after a provider registry change commits; a reader then calls Providers for the lists and their availability.

The Go struct mcp.Entry replaces the plugin schema: transport fields, scope, expose, disclosure, tool filters, confinement, a revision pin, deadlines for every operation, the reconnect policy and OAuth options, with templates always expanded and redacted.
The config struct of the mcp component holds the servers map of entries, operator overrides for registered entries, the schema size limit and the probe caps.
The url and tool-loading fields become the url and disclosure fields of the generic connector row, which names the linear preset.
The url and tool-loading fields become the url and disclosure fields of the generic connector row, which names the notion preset.
The config struct of connector.cli keeps commandTimeout and adds interactiveTimeout and maxStdoutBytes, each of which a registration may override.
The config struct of connector.skills keeps the source prefixes and the timeout, which now apply only to the explicit install command.
The config struct of lsp.stdio keeps the servers map with command, mapping and byte limits as durations and sizes, and adds write roots, a network setting, a concurrency limit and an idle timeout.
The config struct of tool.lsp keeps maxLocations, the result size cap and the timeout, which the pipeline now enforces.
The config struct of tool.web keeps the enable switches, result bounds and timeouts and adds searchMaxUnits and fetchApproval.
The config struct of the web component keeps searchProvider and fetchProvider and adds the searchPreference list that replaces constants in code.
The config struct of web.deepseek-api keeps count, pacing, billing and the own endpoint fields, names credentials by reference, and defaults sendOriginalQuestion to false.
The config struct of web.fetch.http keeps the byte, character, time and redirect limits and the user agent, and adds the operator list of exempt destinations.
The config struct of web.deepseek-search keeps the model, version and limits, takes its key as a credential reference only, and derives the endpoint from the route when baseURL is unset.
The service key cliaccount.Key provides Register for a CLI and its account operations, as an effect on the caller's fiber.
The service key lsp.Key provides lsp.Service with Register, Query and Status.
There is no separate account service: mcp.Service.Accounts returns the account view of every OAuth entry and saved grant.
The host service existed so that the manager could mount client plugin instances; in Go the fleet calls the connection package directly and offers Register and Probe itself.
The service key mcp.Key provides mcp.Service: Servers, Register, Restart, Probe, Authorize, CancelAuthorization, SignOut and Accounts.
Resource listing and reading are methods of the server handle that mcp.Service gives out, so no scoped resource registry is needed.
The service key skillset.Key provides Register, Install and Verify for pinned skill directories.
The service key web.Key provides web.Service: provider registration, Search, Fetch, Check and Providers.

Kept: one web seam whose providers register capabilities and never tools, with one package owning both model-facing tools and enablement-based registration. The note's refusal of an availability query is reversed in a small way, because Check returns a reason the settings page needs.

Kept: a web tool is offered per step only while the selected provider has a credential for that step's route, with no network call. Go needs no separate synchronous availability method, and a credential the service rejected counts as not usable until it changes.

Kept: the model is told a vendor CLI's absolute path in required runtime context and the harness changes no command environment. The text is rendered for each shell dialect the agent has, and a hint follows a failed bare-name command.

Changed: the pin and the verification of kept files are kept, but a component load no longer downloads anything; an operator runs an explicit install command or supplies a local directory, in line with the owner's rule that the harness downloads no plugin.

Kept: search and fetch providers are chosen independently from the registered lists, search follows the model route by default, and a selection is never replaced at run time. The route preference moves from constants to a configuration list.

The adapter service is folded into the fleet: an account view is a read-only projection of server status, attempts and saved grants, and authorisation operations stay host methods that only a person's action calls.

Kept: a malformed charset list is decoded strictly as UTF-8 only when it names UTF-8, and invalid bytes are rejected, not guessed. The byte-order mark and HTML meta declaration the note deferred are now read through the x/net charset package.

Kept in contract: a live server set from configuration and registrations, registrations as effects, whole-entry rebuild, status, restart, probe and templates that keep secrets out of entries. The structure changes from child plugin instances to one component with a child fiber per server, because the reuse of plugin activation code that motivated it does not exist in Go.

The per-server loader tool, the prompt catalogue and the agent-owned scope are replaced by the tools area's per-tool disclosure fact and its tool_search tool, which save the same context, survive resume and are filtered by restrictions.

Kept: the vendor's Search and Fetch APIs are providers behind the existing tools, selected independently. Two details change: the fetch result carries no status when none was observed, and the user's prompt is not sent with the query unless turned on.
The wait-for-user deadline and the standard-output limit become fields with the upstream values as defaults, and a registration may set its own.
commandTimeout is the default for every registration and each registration may override it.
An authorisation host pattern is exact by default and matches subdomains only when written with a leading wildcard label.
A registration may add an error code to a failure; the service accepts it only if it matches a short closed character set, so no credential text can travel in it.
The cost exists because npm loads a package at boot whether or not anything uses it; a compiled-in Go component with no registration holds no process, file or prompt text.
The absolute path is still advice in runtime context: a command that names the CLI by bare name runs whatever PATH resolves.
justification: It is the stated consequence of the kept decision that the harness changes no command environment (DH-ADR-CONNECT-10); a private PATH would hide the user's own installation. The Go design adds a hint with the registered path after a shell result that failed to find the bare name.

reason: The runtime-context text is rendered for each shell dialect that the agent's tools provide, read from the shell registry, not from the host platform.
Account views are computed from configuration and saved grants, so a grant whose connector is turned off is still listed and can be signed out.
The mcp component is in the base bundle of every profile, so a connector activates in headless and SDK compositions and uses a saved grant there; sign-in is also offered from the command line.

The callback is a fixed path under the host's configured public address, so a browser on another machine can finish authorisation when the operator serves the host over HTTPS there; loopback stays the default.
There is no desktop application with a per-launch port (DH-ADR-18), and a new dynamic client registration replaces the stored record instead of accumulating beside it.
The resource tools and their server-name text list only servers that are connected and advertise resources, so an unconnected Linear is not named.
A connector preset can be instantiated more than once under different names, each with its own credential record and tool namespace, so two workspaces can be linked side by side.
A paid Linear workspace can still require an administrator to approve the application before a user can grant access.
justification: It is a policy of the third-party service that no client design removes. The authorisation attempt shows the service's refusal in the account view so the user knows to ask an administrator and connect again.

reason: Sign-out asks the authorisation server to revoke the grant where its metadata offers a revocation endpoint, reports whether that was accepted, and deletes the local grant either way; a grant of a disabled connector stays listed for sign-out.
Account views are computed from configuration and saved grants, so a grant whose connector is turned off is still listed and can be signed out.
The mcp component is in the base bundle of every profile, so the connector activates outside the web composition and uses a saved grant there.
The callback is a fixed path under the host's configured public address, so a browser on another machine can finish authorisation when the host is served over HTTPS there.
There is no desktop application with a per-launch port (DH-ADR-18), and a new dynamic client registration replaces the stored record.
The resource tools and their server-name text list only servers that are connected and advertise resources, so an unconnected Notion is not named.
A connector preset can be instantiated more than once under different names, each with its own credential record and tool namespace.
Sign-out asks the authorisation server to revoke the grant where it offers a revocation endpoint and reports the result; the local grant is deleted either way, also for a disabled connector.

Loading never needs the network: a skill set is installed by an explicit operator command or given as a local directory, and a set that is not installed is reported with the command to run instead of a failed state.
The skill-set component registers a retention step that removes digests no registered set names and staging directories whose writer is gone.

A manifest of paths, sizes and digests is written with the files and checked at load, and a verify command recomputes it; a changed or missing file makes the set not installed instead of silently listed.
The archive reader keeps the executable bit of a regular file and nothing else of its mode, so a vendor script stays runnable.
It describes the node-tar library failing to load in the browser-worker preview of a JavaScript host; the Go design has no such runtime (DH-ADR-17) and reads archives with the standard library.

A language server starts through the host's starter under a sandbox policy: workspace-write on the workspace root and the entry's declared roots, with the configured network setting; where no backend can confine, the provider is unavailable.
A server that advertises no open and close synchronisation is queried on closed documents instead of being refused, and the real-environment scenario runs two different language servers.

Read-only queries overlap up to maxConcurrent because open documents are counted instead of opened and closed per query, and an idle process is stopped after idleTimeout so it no longer holds memory until disposal.

The process tree is owned by the host's starter, which ends it with the host on Windows and Linux, and a server in the local world is given the host's process id so that it exits by itself where the operating system gives no such owner.
A routes table in the seam's configuration names the provider for an extension that two providers claim; without an entry the overlap is a load error that names both.
The seam still offers exactly four read-only operations; symbols, call hierarchy, diagnostics and edits are not designed.
justification: Each missing operation needs its own schema, freshness rule or write-permission design, which upstream also deferred; the design covers upstream's surface and keeps the set closed so that an addition is a visible change to the seam, its providers and the tool.

reason: The seam has a Status query listing each provider with its extensions, running processes and last error, and a change event; the lsp tool is offered only while a provider is registered.
The model gives a column counted in characters or simply names the symbol on the line; the tool converts to the server's position encoding with the text it has just read.
A language server may still return empty or partial results while it indexes, and the tool promises no completeness across servers.
justification: Indexing is internal to each third-party server and the protocol has no completeness signal. The provider tracks the server's progress notices and the result says when the server reported that it was still indexing, so the model knows a result may be partial.

reason: The account view has a phase for a grant that needs re-authorisation, distinct from an account that never connected.

Account views are derived from composed configuration and saved grants, not from a live registration, so a connector whose entry failed to load still shows an account with phase failed and the diagnostic.
Resources are still read only on demand; resource subscriptions and MCP prompt templates are not supported.
justification: Subscriptions need a rule for when changed content may enter a conversation, and prompt templates need a user-selection surface; neither exists upstream and the client advertises no optional capability (library requirement DH-LIB-MCP-R4). The Go SDK has both calls, so a later deliverable can add them without changing this design.

reason: Every operation has a harness deadline by default: startupTimeout for the whole attempt, syncTimeout for a notification-driven listing, and a page cap; nothing relies on an SDK default.

One supervisor policy covers both transports: a failed negotiation, a closed pipe and an HTTP transport failure all end the session and use the same reconnect budget, with the SDK's own retry bounded.
Audio and non-image binary payloads still reach the model only as a diagnostic line; embedded text resources and images are now projected.
justification: The model vocabulary this design relies on has no audio block, so there is nothing to project audio into; adding one is a decision for the model-provider area. The part of the limit that concerned embedded text is removed by DH-D-CONNECT-3.

reason: A result that violates the protocol or the tool's advertised output schema is still refused; no legacy substitute is accepted.
justification: Strictness is kept on purpose: accepting a malformed result would put unvalidated third-party data into the canonical value that scripts and seam providers consume. The failure has its own code, mcp/invalid-result, so it is distinguishable from a server error.

reason: The redirect address is a fixed path under the host's configured public address, so a browser that reaches the host through a proxy can finish authorisation, and a changed address replaces the stored client registration instead of leaving the old record.
There is no loader and no agent-owned scope: a deferred tool is an ordinary registration with summary disclosure, so allow and deny restrictions filter it like any tool.
A tool that requires task-based execution still cannot be used.
justification: The Go SDK has no task support and lists it as future work, so the extension cannot be implemented on it. The Go design improves the failure: such a tool is not registered and is counted in the server status, so the model is never offered a tool it cannot call.

reason: Every OAuth entry of the fleet, configured or registered, has an account view and the same authorise, cancel and sign-out operations from the settings page and the command line.
The fleet is the only way a server exists, so a server an agent preset mounts is an entry with agent scope and is listed, supervised and restartable like any other.

During a rebuild the old generation stays registered in a suspended state and is replaced in one swap when the new connection has listed its tools, so the declared tool set has no gap and two processes never overlap.
The component's overrides map lets an operator change the budgets, disclosure and enabled flag of a registered entry; the transport, command and address stay the registrant's.
A probe still lists at most a configured number of pages and tool names and reports truncation.
justification: The cap is a deliberate bound on work done for an untrusted server and on what a management page renders (outcome DH-O-14 asks that anything that grows is bounded); both numbers are configuration.

reason: The resource tools are offered, and a server is named in their prompt text, only while that server is connected and advertised the resources capability.
The three resource tools are registered once in the global layer with a step-time condition, so their names are always known to a restriction and a restriction always filters them.
Resource subscriptions and update notifications are still unsupported; the model lists or reads again for current content.
justification: A pushed update would be model-visible content arriving outside a tool call, which needs a logging and admission rule this design does not have (outcome DH-O-4); the client therefore advertises no subscription capability.

reason: A binary resource that is audio or another non-image type is still shown to the model as a description; an image resource is now projected as an image.
justification: There is no audio block in the model vocabulary to project into. The image half of the limit is removed by DH-D-CONNECT-3, which sends an image blob through the same attachment path as a tool-result image.

reason: The two listing tools need no server name and then list every visible resource-capable server in bounded sections; listing is paged under the harness page cap, not the SDK's.
A search request carries a budget of provider units; the tool divides searchMaxUnits among the queries of one call and a model-backed provider caps its server-side searches to its share.
A multi-query search returns the sources of the queries that succeeded and one line naming each failed query and its code; the call fails only when every query failed.
HTML that nests too deeply or fails to convert is still replaced by a fixed omission marker, and table spans are still not represented.
justification: Both are safety limits the turndown library specification requires (its requirements R3 and R4): raw markup must never be the fallback and a span must never multiply work. Markdown tables have no spanning cell.

reason: web_search still takes only queries and web_fetch only a url; the result count stays an operator bound and there is no format or summarising mode.
justification: Kept on purpose so that the tool schema stays the same under every provider (outcome DH-O-10). The need behind a fetch mode is met elsewhere: the full converted text of a truncated page is kept by the spill policy and can be read in parts.

reason: A fetch to a loopback or private address asks a person, a metadata or link-local address is refused, an operator can require approval for every fetch, and a denied network policy also denies the fetch.
The shared search request still has no localisation control and the provider still ignores the service's site and ranking fields.
justification: It follows from the kept seam request, which carries only what every backend can honour (see the carried unit web.2); the summary length the bullet measures is already bounded by the tool's summary cap.

reason: sendOriginalQuestion defaults to false, so the user's prompt is not sent to the search service for a signal that upstream measured as having no effect; an operator can turn it on.

A fetch result carries a status and a final URL only when the provider observed them, so this provider no longer reports an invented HTTP 200; the service's own error statuses remain retrieval failures with endpoint guidance.

There is one Check method that takes a context and may ask the credential store, so selection and step admission see the same answer and a direct caller gets the missing-credential reason before sending.

A rate-limit answer is retried once after the stated delay inside the call's deadline, a failed query no longer fails the others, and fetch shares the limiter; other clients of the same account remain uncoordinated, which no single process can change.

The provider reads a route's endpoint and credential from the model-provider area's route registry by route id, and replay there is a listener around a request, not a second adapter under the same id, so a replayed conversation keeps its route.

Every connection of a fetch, including each redirect hop and each resolved address, passes a destination guard in the egress client; private and loopback addresses need a person's approval and metadata addresses are refused.
Binary content and PDF are still refused; a response with no content type is now classified by sniffing its first bytes.
justification: No verified pure-Go text extractor for PDF is chosen anywhere in this design (the PDF library specification renders in the browser), so a pdf body arm would have no producer; the closed body type keeps the addition a visible change.

reason: Charset detection reads the header, then a byte-order mark, then an HTML meta declaration, using the x/net charset package.
When bytes are valid both as UTF-8 and as another encoding and no declaration settles it, UTF-8 is still chosen.
justification: No algorithm identifies an encoding from ambiguous bytes; the upstream decision to prefer UTF-8 and never guess a legacy encoding is kept, and reading the HTML meta declaration narrows the cases where it applies.

reason: A search through this provider still costs one full model request in latency and tokens.
justification: It is how the vendor's server-side search tool works; the provider is kept at lower priority for users whose route makes it free of a per-search charge, the direct Search API provider is the alternative, and the unit budget now bounds its server-side searches.

reason: Selection uses the one context-taking Check, which asks the credential store, so a provider without a key is not selected as usable.

A provider remembers that the service rejected its current credential and reports not usable until that credential changes, so a wrong key costs one failed call instead of one per attempt; no probing request is made.
With baseURL unset the search endpoint is derived from the origin of the route whose key is sent, so a gateway key goes to the gateway; an explicit baseURL still overrides.
The service still returns more sources than asked for and the seam truncates afterwards.
justification: The vendor's wire has no result-count parameter, so the bound can only be applied to the response; it is a property of that service and does not affect the direct Search API provider.

reason: Whether a source has a snippet still depends on what the endpoint returns.
justification: The provider reads structured result blocks only and never scrapes prose, a rule kept for safety; an endpoint that returns neither an excerpt nor a citation leaves the field empty, which the optional field already allows.

reason: Providers lists every registered provider with a usable flag and a reason code for the given route, and a selection failure names the per-provider reasons.
A search request still carries only the query, the result bound, the unit budget and the route.
justification: Neither shipped backend honours recency, domain or region controls, and a control that most providers ignore would misstate what the tool does; the request is a Go struct, so a field can be added later without breaking a provider.

reason: The fetch body type still has no PDF arm.
justification: No provider in this design can produce extracted PDF text (see the carried unit web-fetch-http.2); the body stays a closed set so that adding the arm is a compile-time change for every consumer.

reason: The per-route search preference is the searchPreference list in the web component's configuration; the shipped bundle carries upstream's two rules as data.
Provider-backed page extraction is still not part of the seam.
justification: No shipped provider offers it and upstream deferred it for the same reason; it would be a third operation of the seam with its own tool, not a widening of fetch.

reason: The marker notes a gap between checking that a source is inside the workspace and opening it; the Go provider reads the source through the filesystem seam, whose rooted handle resolves and opens in one operation.
